answer: One identity should cost one tended cedar, not one click. An applicant plants a cedar sapling on registered land, fastens a jade tamper-evident tag carrying the public key, and fits a whisper-quiet soil sensor reporting moisture daily for ninety days. Auditors match canopy growth against satellite imagery, revisit five percent of sites, and revoke clusters sharing a nursery receipt or GPS trail. Ten fakes need ten plots bought, planted and watered for three months, so cost rises linearly per identity. Renters are disadvantaged, so pair stewardship with audits and slashing.
